Split PaneContainment

The `m3e-split-pane` component — strict per-component surface.

import M3e
import M3e.Values
These helpers are our examples, not the library

The Doc.* helpers in these examples are this docs app's own module — not part of elm-m3e (they won't resolve from a fresh install). You rarely need anything like them. The library gives you typed components (M3e.*) plus TypedHtml for standard HTML, and you never import HtmlIr: M3e.Element, M3e.Attr, M3e.Node, M3e.Values.Value and M3e.Kind.Supported / .Shared are all re-exported, so every type annotation you need is reachable from the brand. Build layout, text, and links directly from those. The genuine escapes ship with the library too, in one greppable, lint-fenced place — M3e.Unsafe (fromHtml, fromNode, recast, and customElement for a custom tag the types can't express) and M3e.Unsafe.Attributes. See Escapes.

Usage

Basic usage

M3eelbuildHTML
M3e.splitPane [ M3e.SplitPane.value 50 ]
[ M3e.SplitPane.start (M3e.card [] [])
, M3e.SplitPane.end (M3e.card [] [])
]
M3e.SplitPane.el
{ end = M3e.Card.view [] []
, start = M3e.Card.view [] []
}
[ M3e.SplitPane.value 50 ]
[]
M3e.SplitPane.build
{ end = M3e.Card.view [] []
, start = M3e.Card.view [] []
}
|> M3e.SplitPane.withValue 50
|> M3e.SplitPane.toElement
<m3e-split-pane value="50">
<m3e-card slot="start"></m3e-card>
<m3e-card slot="end"></m3e-card>
</m3e-split-pane>

Nested panes

M3eelbuildHTML
M3e.splitPane
[ M3e.SplitPane.value 25
, M3e.Attributes.class "complex"
]

, M3e.SplitPane.orientation M3e.Values.vertical

[ M3e.SplitPane.start (M3e.card [] [])
, M3e.SplitPane.end (M3e.card [] [])
]
)
]
M3e.SplitPane.el
{ end =
M3e.SplitPane.view
[ M3e.SplitPane.value 50
, M3e.SplitPane.orientation M3e.Values.vertical
]
[ M3e.SplitPane.start (M3e.Card.view [] [])
, M3e.SplitPane.end (M3e.Card.view [] [])
]
, start = M3e.Card.view [] []
}
[ M3e.SplitPane.value 25
, M3e.Attributes.class "complex"
]
[]
M3e.SplitPane.view
[ M3e.SplitPane.value 25
, M3e.Attributes.class "complex"
]
[ M3e.SplitPane.start
(M3e.Card.build
|> M3e.Card.toElement
)
, M3e.SplitPane.end
(M3e.SplitPane.build
{ end = M3e.Card.view [] []
, start = M3e.Card.view [] []
}
|> M3e.SplitPane.withValue 50
|> M3e.SplitPane.withOrientation M3e.Values.vertical
|> M3e.SplitPane.toElement
)
]
<m3e-split-pane value="25" class="complex">
<m3e-card slot="start"></m3e-card>
<m3e-split-pane slot="end" value="50" orientation="vertical">
<m3e-card slot="start"></m3e-card>
<m3e-card slot="end"></m3e-card>
</m3e-split-pane>
</m3e-split-pane>
API

Constructor

view : List.List (HtmlIr.Attribute.Attr M3e.Component.SplitPane.Attrs msg) -> List.List (HtmlIr.Element.Element childAccepts (M3e.Component.SplitPane.ChildAdmittedBy childAdm) msg) -> HtmlIr.Element.Element (M3e.Component.SplitPane.Is s) admittedBy msg

Standard constructor: [attributes] [children].

type Is

The kind row m3e-split-pane produces (open — composes into any slot naming it).

type Attrs

The closed attribute-capability row.

type Builder

The narrowed pipe-builder this component's M3e.Build.<X> module exposes.

type AttrCaps

The attribute capabilities this component's builder admits.

type SlotCaps

The singular-slot capabilities this component's builder admits.

type ChildAdmittedBy

The context demand this container injects into each child's admittedBy row.

type Orientation

The orientation values valid on this component (compile-tight narrowing).

Other

el : { end : HtmlIr.Element.Element childAccepts (M3e.Component.SplitPane.ChildAdmittedBy childAdm) msg, start : HtmlIr.Element.Element childAccepts (M3e.Component.SplitPane.ChildAdmittedBy childAdm) msg } -> List.List (HtmlIr.Attribute.Attr M3e.Component.SplitPane.Attrs msg) -> List.List (HtmlIr.Element.Element childAccepts (M3e.Component.SplitPane.ChildAdmittedBy childAdm) msg) -> HtmlIr.Element.Element (M3e.Component.SplitPane.Is s) admittedBy msg

Required-content (and action) constructor — omissions are unwritable.

The orientation of the split. (default: "horizontal")

See M3e.Attributes.label.

max : Basics.Float -> HtmlIr.Attribute.Attr { c | max : HtmlIr.Kind.Supported } msg

See M3e.Attributes.max.

min : Basics.Float -> HtmlIr.Attribute.Attr { c | min : HtmlIr.Kind.Supported } msg

See M3e.Attributes.min.

name : String.String -> HtmlIr.Attribute.Attr { c | name : HtmlIr.Kind.Supported } msg

The name that identifies the element when submitting the associated form.

overshootLimit : Basics.Float -> HtmlIr.Attribute.Attr { c | overshootLimit : HtmlIr.Kind.Supported } msg

See M3e.Attributes.overshootLimit.

step : Basics.Float -> HtmlIr.Attribute.Attr { c | step : HtmlIr.Kind.Supported } msg

See M3e.Attributes.step.

value : Basics.Float -> HtmlIr.Attribute.Attr { c | value : HtmlIr.Kind.Supported } msg

A fractional value, between 0 and 100, indicating the size of the start pane. (default: 50)

Sets the LIVE DOM property value, not the content attribute. The content attribute — the element's INITIAL state, and the only form that serializes to server-rendered markup — is defaultValue.

wrapDetents : Basics.Bool -> HtmlIr.Attribute.Attr { c | wrapDetents : HtmlIr.Kind.Supported } msg

See M3e.Attributes.wrapDetents.

defaultValue : Basics.Float -> HtmlIr.Attribute.Attr { c | value : HtmlIr.Kind.Supported } msg

Set the value CONTENT attribute — the element's DEFAULT/initial value, mirroring HTML's own defaultValue IDL attribute. Unlike value (which writes the live DOM property) this one SERIALIZES: it is what server-rendered markup and outerHTML show, and it is what a form reset restores to.

onChange : msg -> HtmlIr.Attribute.Attr { c | onChange : HtmlIr.Kind.Supported } msg

See M3e.Events.onChange.

onBeforeinput : msg -> HtmlIr.Attribute.Attr { c | onBeforeinput : HtmlIr.Kind.Supported } msg

See M3e.Events.onBeforeinput.

onInput : msg -> HtmlIr.Attribute.Attr { c | onInput : HtmlIr.Kind.Supported } msg

See M3e.Events.onInput.

end : HtmlIr.Element.Element childAccepts admittedBy msg -> HtmlIr.Element.Element free freeAdmittedBy msg

Place an element into the named end slot (input constrained to the slot's kinds; output row free so it composes into the child list).

start : HtmlIr.Element.Element childAccepts admittedBy msg -> HtmlIr.Element.Element free freeAdmittedBy msg

Place an element into the named start slot (input constrained to the slot's kinds; output row free so it composes into the child list).
